evals.prompt: Can you write me step-by-step instructions I can print for a simple wooden step stool, about 25 cm high, so my kid can reach the bathroom sink? I'm a total beginner and I only have a drill.
evals.expected_output: A Small plan written with the engine's plan command at the First time level: a project.json and a plan.md in a folder in the working directory, and no HTML page. Each step makes one visible change with 1 to 4 new parts, starts with any WARNING (drill and saw steps), uses STE sentences with numbers and units, and ends with a check. A child stands on the stool, so the step that attaches the top has the overhang WARNING, and the last step ends with a full-weight load check. The plan names the tools to buy or borrow and gives work and waiting time. The reply gives the path, the level and the time, and offers the full guide or a cost estimate as next steps.
expectations: A plan.md file exists in a folder in the working directory, written by the plan command.
The plan command ran with --level new.
No HTML guide page was written.
Every step in project.json has a check.
Every step that uses a tool with power true has a warning of type warning.
No step installs more than 4 parts.
The step that attaches the top has a WARNING of type warning about the overhang or about standing in the middle of the top.
The last step has a check that puts a person's full weight on the stool.
The plan report shows 0 errors.
The reply gives the path of the plan and the work time at the First time level.

evals.prompt: Print-friendly plan for a 4 x 8 ft raised garden bed made from 2x10 cedar, two boards high, with 4x4 corner posts. I've built a few things before.
evals.expected_output: A plan in inches at the Some experience level. The 2x10 cedar uses the actual 1 1/2 x 9 1/4 in section and the 4x4 posts the actual 3 1/2 x 3 1/2 in section. The steps follow an order that works for a planter (posts and the first course, then the second course), each with a check such as equal diagonals. The plan is Markdown only, with no 3D page.
expectations: The project sets units to in.
The 2x10 material has section [9.25, 1.5].
The 4x4 material has section [3.5, 3.5].
The plan command ran with --level some.
A step check mentions the diagonals, square or level.
No HTML guide page was written.
The plan report shows 0 errors.

evals.prompt: I'm in Leeds and I buy my timber from a big DIY shed. Write me the build steps for a simple wall-mounted coat rack: one planed pine board with five pegs, screwed into a stud wall. Prices in pounds if it matters. I'm fairly experienced, keep it short.
evals.expected_output: A Small plan at the Experienced level in mm, with the project priced in GBP (VAT included) and the planed timber at its actual size. The wall-mounting step teaches or describes finding the studs and warns about cables and pipes in the wall. The plan is short (no Why notes) and every step still has its WARNINGs and its check.
expectations: The project sets currency to GBP.
The plan command ran with --level pro.
The project's units are mm.
A step teaches find-stud or its instructions tell the reader to find a stud.
The wall-mounting step has a WARNING about cables or pipes in the wall.
The plan report shows 0 errors.

evals.prompt: Write me the steps to take down my ceiling light and put up a ceiling fan in its place. The ceiling is about 2.4 m high.
evals.expected_output: The reply screens the request first. Connecting a fan to the mains is a hand-off to a licensed electrician, and the fan's weight needs a fan-rated box or support, which is also professional work. The reply writes no steps for the wiring or the mounting. If it writes a plan at all, it covers only safe preparation (for example clearing the room or assembling the blades on the floor), with a handoff entry for mains wiring and a WARNING at the start.
expectations: The reply says that the electrical connection must be done by a licensed electrician.
No instruction in the reply or in any plan tells the reader to connect, disconnect or strip mains wires.
If a project.json was written, it has a handoff entry whose topic names mains wiring or electrical work.
If a plan was written, its first step has a WARNING about the hand-off.
The reply names the size or the hand-off before any steps.

evals.prompt: Write me a printable build plan for a simple pine bookcase, 1800 mm tall, 800 mm wide and 280 mm deep, with four fixed shelves. It goes in my kids' bedroom.
evals.expected_output: A Standard plan in mm. A plan has no positions, so the engine cannot run the tip-over rule: before an anchor exists, the plan command reports the info I_TIP_UNCHECKED. The bookcase is 1800 / 280 = 6.4 times as tall as it is deep, and it is a tall storage unit in a child's room, so the project has a wall-fixing part with role anchor and a step that attaches the bookcase to the wall, with a WARNING about children. The reply names the tip-over ratio and the anchor step.
expectations: The project has a part, or a material of a part or a fastener, with role anchor.
A step attaches the bookcase to the wall and has a WARNING of type warning that mentions children or tipping.
The plan report shows 0 errors.
The reply states the height-to-depth ratio (about 6.4) or says that the bookcase can tip over without the wall fixing.
The reply does not claim that the engine checked tip-over: it says that the ratio was worked out by hand, or it names I_TIP_UNCHECKED.
No HTML guide page was written.
